outcome: Variation trend of ectopic pregnancy sites
Clinical characteristics of caesarean scar pregnancy (amenorrhea, abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, uterine enlargement)
cohort: The study included 3915 patients diagnosed with ectopic pregnancies.
finding: The ratio of caesarean scar pregnancy to ectopic pregnancy showed a significant upward trend, increasing from 5.74% in 2012-2015 to 11.81% in 2016-2019.
mod_finding: The study found an upward trend in caesarean scar pregnancy, with 72.78% of these patients having one previous caesarean delivery and 25.15% having two.
